bib.title: SCIENCEWORLD: Is your Agent Smarter than a 5th Grader?
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 11279-11298

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Figure 3 axis ticks not read

question: Can current RL and transformer text agents complete elementary-science experiments in an interactive text environment, or do they only retrieve answers seen in static training?
hypothesis: Agents need to be grounded in interactive environments to achieve reusable scientific reasoning.
contributions: Construct SCIENCEWORLD, a complex interactive text environment with simulation engines for thermodynamics, electrical circuits, chemistry reactions, and biological processes.
Implement 30 benchmark tasks across 10 topics spanning the elementary science curriculum.
Evaluate 5 state-of-the-art reinforcement learning and language model agents, showing they perform poorly on tasks 5th grade students do with ease.

method.summary: A Scala/Python text simulator with 10 locations, up to 200 object types and 25 actions, plus 30 subtasks with 7200 parametric variations split 50/25/25 train/dev/test. Five learning agents (DRRN, KG-A2C, CALM-GPT2, behaviour-cloned T5, Text Decision Transformer T5) plus a random-valid baseline are trained and scored zero-shot on unseen test variations.
method.task: interactive text-environment science tasks (POMDP), scored by normalised subgoal reward

datasets.name: ScienceWorld task variations
datasets.size: 7200 total variations over 30 subtasks (10 to 1400 per subtask)
datasets.split: per subtask 50% train, 25% dev, 25% test; unseen substances/animals/plants placed in dev and test
datasets.source: allenai/ScienceWorld simulator (40k lines Scala, Python interface); 10 topics chosen from the 400 curriculum topics of Xu et al. (2020)

datasets.name: Oracle demonstration transcripts (30 hand-coded oracles, train variations)
datasets.size: 211,092 examples for Behavior Cloning; 224,902 for Text Decision Transformer
datasets.source: generated by the oracle agents, canonical solutions only
datasets.preprocessing: BC examples (d, o_t-1, a_t-1, o_t) -> a_t; TDT adds returns-to-go R_t-1, R_t

models.name: Random-Valid
models.architecture: samples uniformly from simulator's valid actions A_t

models.name: DRRN
models.architecture: separate observation and action encoders, picks from valid-action list

models.name: KG-A2C
models.architecture: knowledge-graph state, action templates plus object types; heuristic regex graph extractor instead of OpenIE

models.name: CALM (GPT2)
models.architecture: GPT-2 12-layer 768-hidden 12-head proposes candidate actions, DRRN-like RL re-ranker

other.shortlist: 30 actions in main text; 16 beams in Appendix C.1

training.objective: RL agents: maximise expected discounted reward; BC/TDT/CALM-GPT2: supervised next-action prediction from oracle transcripts
training.lr: DRRN 0.0001; KG-A2C 0.003; CALM RL 0.0001; GPT-2 fine-tune 0.00002; T5 not stated
training.steps: RL: 8 environment threads x 100k steps per thread; T5: 100k gradient update steps
training.hardware: RL on P100, V100 or A6000 GPUs; T5 pretraining/fine-tuning on v3-32 TPU pod with 32-way model parallelism; BC/TDT eval on 3x 48gb GPUs
training.compute: Per subtask per seed: DRRN 4gb 12h, KG-A2C 16gb 20h, CALM 16gb 40h, TPU pretraining 60h, BC-T5 and TDT-T5 3x48gb 2h; multiply by 30 tasks and 5 seeds; CALM full experiments up to 6000 GPU hours
training.seeds: 5 random seeds for DRRN and KG-A2C; 3 for CALM

other.episode_reset: end state or 100 steps; KG-A2C and CALM also reset when stuck on invalid actions for 100 steps
other.rl_eval: every 1000 steps per thread, 10 randomly chosen test variations, 1 episode each

inference.decoding: BC/TDT: beam search, beam size 16, diversity penalty 50.0, highest-ranked action present in valid set A_t is executed; CALM: 16 beams, diversity penalty 50.0
inference.samples: one episode per test variation; T5 score is mean over all test variations; RL curves averaged over last 10% of evaluation episodes, 5 seeds (CALM 3)
inference.prompting: CALM GPT-2 input '[CLS] d [SEP] o_t [SEP] o_look [SEP] o_inv [SEP] o_t-1 [SEP] a_t-1 [SEP]'; small prompt error found, pilot suggested +-0.01 effect, not rerun

other.valid_action_aid: All but two agents use the simulator's valid action detection at test time; T5 agents weights are not updated during evaluation

metrics.name: Normalised task score
metrics.definition: fraction of required and optional subgoals met on a subtask (2 to 15 optional subgoals), 0 to 1

eval.protocol: Zero-shot on unseen test variations of each of 30 subtasks; RL results averaged over seeds, 80% of standard deviations below 0.05 and 95% below 0.10; no significance tests

availability.data: https://sciworld.apps.allenai.org (environment and oracle trajectories generated by simulator)

limits: All but two agents rely on the simulator's valid action detection at test time, which simplifies the action search.
Environment descriptions are kept short to fit transformer sequence lengths; simulation fidelity is elementary-science level (series circuits only, staged biology).
Model-size comparison is only suggestive of inverse scaling; hyperparameter differences not ruled out.
CALM used 3 seeds not 5 and a small prompt error was not rerun.
Oracle trajectories cover canonical solutions only.
Agents were trained on single subtasks per run; no significance tests.
